description: Uses GameObject.Find("__Pool_Cube_26"), "__Pool_Cube_27", and "__Pool_Cube_28". Valid cube pool names are only __Pool_Cube_01..50? No—the documented allowed names for Find are the actual pool names, but the strict rule explicitly whitelists __Pool_Cube_01..50. However this code also uses plane names __Pool_Plane_04 and __Pool_Plane_05 while the allowed plane pool range is only __Pool_Plane_01..10; those are okay. The critical issue is that these extra finds are not part of the declared object mapping and may not exist in the scene template, causing null-driven missing gameplay objects. Historical failure pattern: relying on undeclared extra pool objects without guaranteed template availability.
fix: Only use pool objects guaranteed by the storyboard/template mapping, or explicitly verify these pool objects exist in the injected template. Add null-safe fallback gameplay that does not depend on __Pool_Cube_26/27/28 existing.

description: Uses ternary operators in multiple places (e.g. iceCount > 0 ? ..., phaseEnterTimes[0] > 0 ? ...). Bridge/Luna hard-limit list is strict and historically many modern C# constructs transpile unreliably; this should be treated as unsupported/risky under strict review.
fix: Replace ternary expressions with explicit if/else assignments before concatenation.

description: Multiple progression-critical interactions require Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) for world pickups/sales/upgrades while movement is driven by joystick. On mobile Luna playables this often blocks progression because CUA interaction is joystick-first and tap timing on world objects is unreliable. Production rule allows proximity auto-collect but forbids skipping interaction; here you should use proximity-based collection/activation for pickups and context interactions, not mouse click gating.
fix: Replace click-gated world interactions with proximity-triggered collection/use (ice chunk, water bottles, apples, selling when near valid passenger, upgrade purchase when standing on station, etc.), while keeping player movement as the required interaction driver.

description: Phase progression is driven by pure numeric thresholds: gold >= 5 && totalSold >= 2, gold >= 8, appleProductCount >= 1 && totalSold >= 4. The documented rule explicitly forbids pure numeric triggers that auto-jump phase. These can advance phases without fresh user interaction.
fix: Gate each phase transition on a player-driven interaction flag in addition to resources, e.g. player used upgrade station, player entered gate trigger, player pressed apple button / sold at apple sell point, then check dwell time.

In Luna review terms this counts as incomplete phase implementation: not all blueprint phases are guaranteed reachable in-template.
fix: Use only guaranteed mapped objects or add robust fallback so every phase remains completable with the base mapped objects alone.

description: Camera.backgroundColor is set twice. Final value is (0.75, 0.82, 0.92), while ground IceField is initially set to (0.75, 0.78, 0.82). The per-channel differences are 0.00, 0.04, 0.10 — none reach the required >= 0.3. If visible geometry fails later, this can present as a near-solid screen and violates the explicit camera/ground contrast rule.
fix: Use a background color differing by at least 0.3 on one RGB channel from the ground, e.g. dark blue/gray like (0.35, 0.45, 0.7) or much darker.

description: Rule 0 must position >= 3 differently-colored objects at y >= -1 in the first frame. This code does place objects, but WaterMachine is a Plane object scaled as a tall 3D machine at y=1.5. In Luna, planes are flat and camera-angled visibility is fragile; relying on it as one of the initial anti-solid-color objects is risky. More importantly, only MainDeck, Player, and PassengerQueueMain are guaranteed strong visible forms; the initial scene should clearly use 3+ robust visible objects. Current setup is borderline and has already weakened the anti-solid-color safeguard.
fix: Ensure at least 3 clearly visible non-plane objects are shown in frame 1 at y >= -1 with distinct colors, e.g. MainDeck, Player, PassengerQueueMain, MainSellPoint.
